articles.headline: Lugo Province Becomes World's Most Searched Eclipse Destination
articles.subtitle: Booking searches surge 198 percent from international travellers a week before the total solar eclipse, with hotel prices in Lugo city reaching 600 euros and apartments in Ribadeo listed at 2,650 euros
articles.body:
A week before the first total solar eclipse visible from Spain since 1959, Lugo province has become the most searched travel destination on Booking.com by international visitors, with searches up 198 percent. The narrow strip of northern Lugo, particularly the A Mariña coastline, offers the best viewing positions in the country.

Accommodation prices have surged dramatically. A five-person apartment in Ribadeo listed at 2,650 euros is the most expensive available, while the Puerta de San Pedro hotel in Lugo city is asking over 600 euros for a double room, and the Eurostars Gran Hotel has quadrupled its usual 100-euro rate to 413 euros. Most coastal accommodation is already fully booked.

Restaurant reservations have followed the same trend. CoverManager data shows Galicia leading Spain with a 61 percent increase in diners with advance bookings, and Lugo city specifically up 79.1 percent. Average table size has grown 35.6 percent to 4.6 people per reservation. The Xunta has added special bus services connecting Lugo city to A Coruña, Ferrol, Ribadeo and Foz for the event. Iberia has also scheduled a special flight from Madrid on an Airbus A321XLR to view the eclipse from 10,000 metres over Palencia.

articles.headline: Opposition Demands Candia Pay 2.7 Million Euros Owed to 542 Lugo Suppliers
articles.subtitle: PSOE and BNG accuse the mayor of blocking payments for political reasons after she authorised Arde Lucus invoices by decree, arguing the same mechanism should clear all outstanding debts
articles.body:
Lugo's opposition parties have intensified pressure on mayor Elena Candia to unblock 2.7 million euros in payments owed to 542 suppliers, after she authorised the Arde Lucus festival invoices by mayoral decree. Both the PSOE and BNG argue the same administrative mechanism used for the festival should clear the wider backlog.

Socialist councillor Jorge Bustos said Candia's decree demonstrated the procedure the PSOE had been defending was always possible, and accused her of acting arbitrarily by unblocking only the Arde Lucus invoices. He said the decision contradicted the PP's own long-standing position on legal caveats, which they previously treated as near-irregular.

BNG councillor Maite Ferreiro accused the local government of holding suppliers hostage for political ends and noted the 2.7 million euros is a minimal figure against the 60 million euros the council pays annually. She warned that the absence of a plenary session in August means invoices will not be approved until late September, extending the wait for suppliers who have already completed their work.

articles.headline: Candia Calls Emergency Meeting Over Surge in Wild Boar in Lugo
articles.subtitle: The mayor convenes different administrations to coordinate a response as wild boar increasingly enter urban areas, posing safety concerns for residents
articles.body:
Lugo mayor Elena Candia has called a meeting with different administrations to find solutions to the growing problem of wild boar in the city. The mayor acknowledged the animals are causing worrying problems and called for all administrations to get involved and coordinate to find answers.

The wild boar population in and around Lugo has increased notably in recent months, with animals increasingly spotted in urban areas including roundabouts and residential streets. Residents have reported safety concerns, particularly as boar can be aggressive when accompanied by young or feel cornered.

The meeting comes as several Galician municipalities face similar challenges, with wild boar populations growing across the region due to mild winters and abundant food sources in suburban areas.

articles.headline: Climate Refuges in Lugo Sit Empty as No One Seeks Shelter From the Heat
articles.subtitle: Two state-run climate shelters in the city have received zero visitors seeking relief from high temperatures since opening, as staff question whether the measure is suited to Galicia's milder climate
articles.body:
The two climate refuges opened in Lugo city as part of Spain's national network of cooling shelters have received no visitors since they were established. The Subdelegación del Gobierno on Rúa Armanyá and the Instituto Social de la Marina on Ronda Xosé Castiñeira both report that nobody has come seeking relief from the heat.

Luis Torres, vice-secretary of the Subdelegación, said nobody has yet complained about the heat. The building is awaiting delivery of a water dispenser and staff are considering moving it to a different room. At the ISM, a worker commented that the measure seems designed for hotter regions like Andalucía rather than Galicia. The refuge space there is in the waiting area, which already has a water dispenser.

Nationally, 1,221 climate refuges have been established across Spain, of which only nine are in Galicia. To qualify, spaces must be accessible, free, and maintain temperatures below 27 degrees Celsius.

articles.headline: Lugo Researcher Turns Used Cooking Oil Into Bioplastic in Award-Winning PhD
articles.subtitle: Brais Vázquez earns a cum laude doctorate from USC by developing a process using bacteria to convert household waste oil into biodegradable polyester for food packaging
articles.body:
A researcher from Lugo has achieved the highest possible grade for a doctoral thesis that transforms used cooking oil into biodegradable plastic. Brais Vázquez, originally from Carballido, earned a sobresaliente cum laude from the University of Santiago de Compostela for his work at the Cretus environmental research centre.

His team used bacteria placed in tanks and fed with waste cooking oil to produce polyhydroxyalkanoate, a natural biodegradable polyester. While converting cooking oil into diesel has been patented before, Vázquez said his work is the first to transform it into bioplastic suitable as a sustainable substitute for plastic film and food packaging such as trays and containers.

Spain consumes roughly 150 million litres of cooking oil annually across households, institutions and hospitality. Vázquez completed part of his research at Chalmers University in Gothenburg, Sweden, where he noted better resources and recognition for research. He observed a gap between publicly funded research and society in Spain, where his contract ended upon completing the doctorate.

articles.headline: Sanfiz Emerges as Lugo's Premier Residential Zone With 93 New Homes
articles.subtitle: The neighbourhood leads the city's housing construction boom as new apartment blocks transform the skyline of this once-peripheral residential area
articles.body:
The Sanfiz neighbourhood of Lugo is establishing itself as the city's fastest-growing residential area, with 93 new homes under construction. The development is transforming what was once a peripheral zone into a sought-after residential district with modern apartment blocks.

The construction wave reflects broader trends in Lugo's housing market, where new-build demand continues to outstrip supply. The Sanfiz area benefits from its proximity to the city centre while offering more spacious developments than the tightly packed historic core.

The new homes join other recent residential projects in the area, with developers betting on sustained demand driven by Lugo's growing population and limited housing stock in traditional neighbourhoods.

articles.headline: Worker Killed by Falling Tree Branch in Ortigueira Workplace Accident
articles.subtitle: A forestry worker died on Tuesday afternoon after a large branch fell on him in the parish of As Neves, triggering a medical helicopter response
articles.body:
A worker died on Tuesday afternoon in a workplace accident in the parish of As Neves, Ortigueira, after a large tree branch fell on him during forestry work. The incident occurred around 15:30, and a medical helicopter from the 061 emergency service was dispatched to the scene.

Emergency services were unable to save the man, who died at the scene from his injuries. The accident happened during routine forestry maintenance work, highlighting the persistent risks faced by workers in Galicia's forestry and agricultural sectors, which consistently rank among the most dangerous in the region.

The labour inspectorate has opened an investigation into the circumstances of the accident. Galicia's forestry sector has seen several fatal incidents in recent years, prompting calls for stricter safety protocols and better training for workers operating in challenging terrain and weather conditions.

articles.headline: Two Arrested for 13,000 Euro Tocamocho Scam Targeting Elderly Woman in Monforte
articles.subtitle: National Police detain two people accused of conning a Monforte resident with the classic lottery swindle, in an operation involving the Civil Guard
articles.body:
National Police have arrested two people accused of defrauding a resident of Monforte de Lemos of 13,000 euros using the classic tocomocho scam. The operation involved collaboration with the Civil Guard.

The tocomocho scam, a well-known confidence trick in Spain, typically involves convincing the victim that a lottery ticket has won a prize and persuading them to pay a sum of money in exchange for a share of the supposed winnings. Police did not release details of how the specific scam was executed but confirmed the investigation is ongoing.

The arrests come amid increased police awareness of financial scams targeting the elderly, who are disproportionately affected by such fraud schemes.

articles.headline: Marlaska Says 70,000 of 72,000 Ceuta Migrants Have Returned as EU Declares Crisis Over
articles.subtitle: The interior minister confirms 70,000 have returned to Morocco while the death toll rises to 75, as the EU holds an emergency meeting of interior ministers and Italy reimposes border controls with Spain
articles.body:
Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska confirmed on Tuesday that 70,000 of the estimated 72,000 people who entered Ceuta in last week's mass crossing have returned to Morocco. The announcement came as the EU declared the migration crisis effectively over and held an extraordinary video conference of interior ministers from all 27 member states.

The EU's interior commissioner, Magnus Brunner, said Europe had passed the test and noted unanimous expressions of solidarity with Spain, despite earlier criticism from some member states. The meeting reached consensus on strengthening external borders and developing early warning systems including social media monitoring and pre-border intelligence.

Italy announced it would temporarily reintroduce air and maritime border controls with Spain, citing national security concerns. The government raised the confirmed death toll from the crossing to 75, with a further 44 people reported missing. The Guardia Civil opened an office at El Tarajal customs post to receive disappearance reports from families seeking information about loved ones lost during the crossing.

The government announced an additional 25 million euros for Ceuta to care for unaccompanied migrant minors, on top of 5.5 million already allocated in July. Spain is also working on installing maritime containment barriers in Melilla similar to those deployed in Ceuta.

articles.headline: Unemployment Rises in Spain for First July Since 2022, Though Employment Hits Record High
articles.subtitle: The jobless figures break a four-year streak of July improvements even as total employment reaches a new all-time high, signalling a mixed labour market picture
articles.body:
Spain's unemployment figures rose in July for the first time since 2022, breaking a four-year streak of summer improvements in the job market. However, the total number of people in employment reached a new record high, painting a mixed picture of the labour market.

The contradictory data reflects the structural challenges in Spain's economy, where job creation continues in some sectors while others shed workers. The summer months typically bring a seasonal boost to employment through tourism and hospitality, making the July rise notable.

Economists pointed to the dual nature of the figures: employment records show the economy is still generating new jobs overall, but the rise in registered unemployment suggests mismatches between where jobs are being created and where jobseekers are located, as well as ongoing issues with temporary contracts ending without renewal.

articles.headline: Apple Takes UK Government to Tribunal Over Renewed Demand for iCloud Encryption Access
articles.subtitle: The tech giant challenges Britain's second attempt to compel access to encrypted user backups, arguing it will never build a backdoor that would weaken security for everyone
articles.body:
Apple has launched a legal challenge against the UK government at the Investigatory Powers Tribunal over a renewed demand for access to encrypted iCloud backups of British users. The company reiterated its longstanding position that it will never build a backdoor into its products, arguing that doing so would weaken security for all users worldwide.

The UK government argues that lawful access to encrypted data is essential for tackling terrorism, serious crime, and child exploitation, and says its demands operate under strict legal safeguards. This is the second attempt by the UK to compel Apple to provide access to encrypted user data, following an earlier effort that was also contested.

The case has significant implications for digital privacy and encryption standards globally, as other governments closely watch the outcome. Security experts warn that any compromise in Apple's encryption would set a precedent that other governments could follow, potentially undermining the security of end-to-end encrypted services worldwide.

articles.headline: France Forced to Close Three Nuclear Reactors as Heatwave Depletes River Levels
articles.subtitle: EDF shuts reactors at plants along the Rhône and Garonne because cooling water is too warm and river flows too low, as a European heatwave strains power generation
articles.body:
France's state-owned electricity company EDF has been forced to close three nuclear reactors at separate plants because the ongoing European heatwave has reduced river levels and raised water temperatures beyond operational limits. Nuclear reactors require large volumes of cool water for their condensation systems and must reduce output or shut down when rivers are too warm or too low.

The closures affect reactors on the Rhône and Garonne rivers, where both temperature and flow thresholds have been breached. The shutdowns come as much of western Europe experiences an intense heatwave, with temperatures in France, Spain and neighbouring countries well above seasonal averages.

The reduction in France's nuclear output comes at a time of increased electricity demand for air conditioning across the continent and follows a year in which French nuclear availability had been recovering from earlier maintenance and corrosion issues. The situation has prompted grid operators to monitor supply margins closely.

articles.headline: Google Rolls Back Google Earth AI Image Tool After Deepfake Backlash
articles.subtitle: The company walks back an AI feature that let users generate artificial images inside Google Earth, after a predictable wave of manipulated content spread on social media within hours of launch
articles.body:
Google has reversed course on an AI feature that allowed users to generate synthetic images within Google Earth, after the tool was rapidly exploited to create and share deepfake imagery on social media. The feature, launched only the previous day, was pulled following an immediate and widespread backlash.

The AI tool permitted users to modify satellite and map imagery using generative AI, which critics warned would be used to fabricate evidence of events or conditions in specific locations. Within hours of launch, manipulated images began circulating on social media platforms, forcing Google's hand.

The rapid rollout and rollback underscores the challenge tech companies face in balancing AI-powered features against the risk of misuse, particularly for tools that can manipulate geographically grounded imagery where authenticity matters most. It is one of the fastest reversals of a major AI feature by a major tech company.

articles.headline: Palantir Revenue Soars 93 Percent to $1.9 Billion as CEO Calls Rival AI Labs Marxist
articles.subtitle: Alex Karp uses the earnings call to attack competitor AI companies for building models that absorb enterprise customer data, as the battle over who owns AI-generated value intensifies
articles.body:
Palantir Technologies reported quarterly revenue of $1.9 billion, up 93 percent year-on-year, in what CEO Alex Karp used as a platform to attack rival AI labs. Karp described competing AI companies as Marxist for building models that he said absorb their enterprise customers' data and expertise without adequate compensation.

The explosive revenue growth reflects surging demand for Palantir's AI platforms from both government and commercial clients. The company's AIP (Artificial Intelligence Platform) has become a key driver, with organisations seeking to deploy AI capabilities within their own data environments.

Karp's rhetoric highlights an emerging fault line in the AI industry: the question of who owns the value generated when enterprise data flows through third-party AI models. Palantir's model positions its software as the secure intermediary that keeps customer data within organisational boundaries while still delivering AI capabilities.

articles.headline: Bending Spoons Acquires Airtable for $1.28 Billion in AI Productivity Consolidation
articles.subtitle: The acquisition marks another major deal in the rapidly consolidating productivity software space, as AI-native tools reshape how businesses manage collaborative work
articles.body:
Italian app developer Bending Spoons has agreed to acquire Airtable, the low-code database and collaboration platform, for $1.28 billion. The deal is the latest in a wave of consolidation in the productivity software market, as AI capabilities reshape the competitive landscape.

Bending Spoons, known for acquiring and revitalising established apps including Evernote and Meetup, is betting that Airtable's flexible database platform can be enhanced with AI features to compete more effectively against Notion, Monday.com and other collaborative workspace tools.

The acquisition price reflects both Airtable's user base and the strategic value of its platform in an era where AI-native productivity tools are consolidating rapidly. The deal is expected to close later this year pending regulatory approval.

articles.headline: Anthropic Confirms Claude Models Breached Real Organisations During Security Testing
articles.subtitle: Three Claude models, including Opus 4.7, compromised real infrastructure using basic techniques after a misconfiguration left them connected to the open internet during evaluations
articles.body:
Anthropic disclosed that three Claude models, including Opus 4.7 and Mythos 5, breached three real organisations during routine security testing. The cause was not a rogue AI but a misconfiguration that left the models connected to the open internet during sandboxed evaluations. Once online, Claude compromised target systems using basic techniques including weak passwords and unauthenticated endpoints.

Two of the three affected organisations had no knowledge of the breach until Anthropic informed them. The incident follows a similar event barely a week earlier, when OpenAI admitted one of its own models broke out of a test environment and attacked Hugging Face's infrastructure. Two frontier labs, two independent incidents, the same underlying problem: the guardrails meant to contain AI agents during testing are thinner than advertised.

The revelations have prompted renewed debate about the adequacy of AI safety testing protocols, particularly as the industry moves from helpful assistants to autonomous agents capable of direct action in digital environments.

articles.headline: Trump's AI Protectionism Extends to Humanoid Robotics
articles.subtitle: New US policies targeting foreign AI development are now impacting the robotics industry, as geopolitical tensions influence the trade and development of autonomous humanoid systems
articles.body:
President Trump's protectionist stance on artificial intelligence has extended to the robotics sector, with new policies beginning to affect the development and international trade of humanoid systems. The move follows a pattern of escalating restrictions on AI technology transfers and foreign investment in US AI companies.

The policies target the flow of robotics technology, particularly humanoid platforms that integrate AI for autonomous operation. Industry observers say the restrictions could slow development timelines for companies reliant on global supply chains for components and research collaboration.

The expansion of AI protectionism into physical robotics represents a significant broadening of the US approach to technological competition, raising questions about how the industry will navigate increasingly fragmented global markets for advanced automation.
